questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “All living things are made up of _____, from the organs in the human body to the parts of plants.”

hints.nudge: The missing word names more than one thing. Read the whole sentence and ask which of them the article is talking about.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cell article.

questions.proof: All living things are made up of cells, from the organs in the human body to the parts of plants.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was thought these were always unicellular but there have been multicellular _____, and today mostly eukaryotes are focused on even when they prefer extreme environments.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “multicellular”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Multicellular (eukaryotic)” part of the Cell article.

questions.proof: It was thought these were always unicellular but there have been multicellular archaea, and today mostly eukaryotes are focused on even when they prefer extreme environments.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ are almost always unicellular, while eukaryotes can be unicellular or multicellular.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “almost”. It names more than one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)” part of the Cell article.

questions.proof: Prokaryotes are almost always unicellular, while eukaryotes can be unicellular or multicellular.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “All _____ and animals are multicellular organisms.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “animals”. It names more than one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Multicellular (eukaryotic)” part of the Cell article.

questions.proof: All plants and animals are multicellular organisms.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ are the nucleus (where DNA is), and mitochondria (where chemical energy is converted).”

hints.nudge: The missing word names more than one thing. Read the whole sentence and ask which of them the article is talking about.
